title: Candy
corePattern: Two-Sided Greedy Constraint Satisfaction and Slope Counting
interviewTips: Ask: must higher-rated child get strictly more than both neighbors, and minimum 1 candy each? Confirm total minimum sum is required.
Trade-off: Two-pass O(n) space is easiest to prove correct; one-pass O(1) space saves memory but needs careful peak handling for up/down slopes.
Edge-case tip: flat ratings [1,1,1], strictly increasing, strictly decreasing, and valley-peak like [1,3,2,2,1] expose max() and peak-adjustment bugs.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Iterative Fixing
approaches.intuition: Start everyone with 1 candy. While any child with higher rating than a neighbor does not have more candies, bump them up. Repeat until stable.
approaches.theory: The constraints are local: ratings[i] > ratings[i-1] implies candies[i] > candies[i-1], and similarly to the right. Starting from all 1s and monotonically increasing only violating positions converges to the minimal feasible assignment. In worst case like decreasing ratings, each full scan propagates values by one position, needing O(n) scans over O(n) elements.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each scan is O(n). In worst case strictly decreasing ratings, values propagate one step per scan, needing O(n) scans.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Extra candies array of size n.

steps: scan1: i=1 rating 3>1 so candies[1]=2, i=2 rating 2<3 no left bump but check right none, candies=[1,2,1] still violates? i=1 vs right: 3>2 and 2>1 ok

approaches.name: Approach 2: Two-Pass Greedy
approaches.intuition: Left neighbor constraint and right neighbor constraint are independent. Satisfy left constraints in one left-to-right pass, then satisfy right constraints right-to-left taking max to preserve left correctness.
approaches.theory: Left pass ensures if ratings[i] > ratings[i-1] then candies[i] = candies[i-1]+1 else 1, which is minimal for left-only constraints. Right pass ensures if ratings[i] > ratings[i+1] then candies[i] = max(candies[i], candies[i+1]+1). Taking max keeps left condition intact while fixing right condition, yielding globally minimal feasible assignment by exchange argument.

timeComplexity.explanation: Two linear scans plus final sum, each O(n).

steps: right pass: i=1 3>2 => max(2,2)=2, i=0 1>3 false

edgeCases: ratings=[1,3,4,5,2] left gives [1,2,3,4,1] right keeps peak, sum 11
ratings=[1,3,2,2,1] needs max to avoid overwriting valley: gives [1,2,1,2,1]

approaches.name: Approach 3: One-Pass Slope Counting O(1) Space
approaches.intuition: Candies follow slopes: increasing run 1,2,3.. and decreasing run ..3,2,1. Only the peak where up meets down needs extra care if down is as long as up.
approaches.theory: Track length of current increasing sequence inc, current decreasing length dec, and last assigned pre. On up/flat, assign pre+1 or 1 and reset dec. On down, dec++ contributes dec candies; if dec == inc, the peak was not tall enough to accommodate the down slope, so increment dec once more to raise the peak. This counts sum on the fly without storing array and equals two-pass result.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear scan, O(1) work per element.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few integer counters, no extra array.

edgeCases: strictly decreasing [5,4,3,2,1] triggers dec==inc adjustment, sum 15
flat [1,1,1] resets to 1 each time, sum 3
peak with equal up/down [1,2,3,2,1] needs peak bump: candies [1,2,3,2,1] sum 9
